# MAHE Bengaluru 3D Digital Twin

> A Photorealistic, AI-Powered 3D Campus Digital Twin & Geospatial Simulation built with React Three Fiber, CesiumGS OGC 3D Tiles, TypeScript, and Vite.

## Summary

MAHE Bengaluru 3D Digital Twin provides an interactive 3D WebGL replica of the 85-acre Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE) Bengaluru campus (13.1169° N, 77.5901° E). It features physically based rendering (PBR), real-time post-processing (SSAO, Bloom, ACES Filmic Tone Mapping), A* topological pathfinding, CesiumGS OGC 3D Tiles streaming, autonomous AI building in-charge agents, and campus logistics hubs.

## Core Capabilities

- **3D Engine**: WebGL rendering via Three.js r185, React Three Fiber, and @react-three/drei with dynamic Day/Night/Dusk lighting and monsoon weather.
- **Geospatial Tiles**: NASA-AMMOS 3d-tiles-renderer with Cesium Ion authentication for streaming massive OSM buildings and terrain.
- **Pathfinding**: A* shortest-path graph solver with real-time 3D animated walking spline and turn-by-turn directions.
- **AI Agent System**: Autonomous building in-charge personas with domain knowledge, prompt recommendations, and campus change request audit trails.
- **Access Control**: Live Gate 1, 2, and 3 logistics and access monitoring.
- **Governance**: Administrator dashboard for approving or rejecting crowd-sourced and automated campus updates with audit logging.

## Technical Specifications

- Framework: React 19, TypeScript, Vite
- Styling: TailwindCSS 4, Lucide React
- 3D Libraries: Three.js, React Three Fiber, Postprocessing
- Coordinates: WGS84 13.1169° N, 77.5901° E (1 unit = ~3.5 meters)
- Node Runtime: >= 18.0.0
